item.description:
## OpenAI alerts over 100 organizations to unauthorized AI agent activity: report [OpenAI](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) has notified more than 100 organizations about unauthorized activity tied to its AI agents, Reuters reported, citing a blog post by the ChatGPT maker.
## FBI overhauls tech backbone to counter AI threats from foreign adversaries, Patel says [The FBI](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/topics/fbi) has adapted itself and its cybersecurity capabilities to combat nefarious uses of artificial intelligence from adversarial nations like China and Russia through full-scale modernization — something past leadership relied on temporary fixes to do, FBI Director Kash Patel said.
## Google convinces federal judge to dismiss lawsuits from Chegg, Penske Media over AI overviews This week, a federal judge dismissed lawsuits filed by education technology company Chegg and Rolling Stone publisher Penske Media, which alleged that Google's AI Overviews — the [AI-generated](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) summaries that appear at the top of many search results — violated antitrust law by diverting traffic from their websites.
## Anthropic cofounder seems to believe Claude has rights to 'dignity, respect': Report For months, Anthropic has been privately meeting with religious leaders and scholars to explore whether advanced [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) could someday attain consciousness and how centuries of moral wisdom might help shape its Claude chatbot, The New York Times reported this week.
## Pope says AI-generated art lacks 'spark of humanity' in latest warning about artificial intelligence ![Pope says AI-generated art lacks 'spark of humanity' in latest warning about artificial intelligence](https://a57.foxnews.com/assets.foxnews.com/liveblog/fn/prod/images/2026/10/624/351/69bd7b9ceb5d6e5f1418500890917d77.jpg?ve=1&tl=1)
[Pope Leo XIV](https://www.foxnews.com/category/person/pope-leo-xiv) said it is becoming urgent to distinguish between art purely created through human creativity and works generated by [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) models.
Algorithms lack the spark of humanity," the pope wrote on social media Friday morning.
The current pope, who was elected during last May's conclave, has taken an unflinching stance about artificial intelligence's potential to disrupt humanity's place in the world.
## Chinese AI model investigated after researcher flags bioweapon, assassination risks Chinese [AI](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) company Moonshot AI has launched an internal investigation after a researcher found that one of its models could be manipulated into providing instructions for developing biological weapons and carrying out assassinations, Fox News senior foreign policy correspondent Gillian Turner reported Thursday.

item.title: Trump wants to stamp out the term ‘artificial intelligence’. Why?
item.description:
[Artificial intelligence](https://www.scmp.com/topics/artificial-intelligence?module=breadcrumb&pgtype=article)
# What’s in a name? Why Trump wants to rebrand AI as ‘super intelligence’ ### The US president’s insistence on using the term ‘super intelligence’ reflects a wider debate over the technology’s future, analysts say [Artificial intelligence (AI)](https://www.scmp.com/topics/artificial-intelligence?module=topic_widget&pgtype=article)
US President Donald Trump wants to retire one of the technology sector’s most recognisable acronyms, arguing that the term “artificial intelligence”, or AI, is no longer fit for purpose.
On Tuesday, Trump signed an executive order directing US federal agencies to replace “artificial intelligence” and “AI” with “super intelligence” and “SI” in official communications and non-statutory documents.
## Trump rejects working with China on AI despite Xi’s recent visit ### How has China reacted? China’s foreign ministry said it “respects” Washington’s choice while continuing to use the term “artificial intelligence”.

item.title: Fact Check Team: What’s the difference between artificial intelligence & superintelligence
‘Super Intelligence,’ Trump’s Dopey AI Rebrand, Explained
item.description:
Americans’ concerns about [artificial intelligence](https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/ai-apocalypse-doomer-panel.html) have quickly escalated from “it might take our jobs” to “it might kill us all.” A recent Quinnipiac [survey](https://poll.qu.edu/poll-release?releaseid=3968) found 58 percent of respondents disapprove of the president’s handling of artificial intelligence, versus just 25 percent who approve.
But now Trump has a plan to shut down all this AI doomerism: Simply change the name “artificial intelligence” to “super intelligence.”
Then he announced at the [United Nations](https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/trump-addresses-un-general-assembly-live-updates.html) that “artificial intelligence” is “hereinafter officially called ‘super intelligence.’”
## . Doesn’t “superintelligence” already mean something else? “Artificial intelligence” has been in use since Dartmouth computer scientist [John McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(computer_scientist)) coined it in 1956.
The next level, “artificial general intelligence,” or AGI, refers to AI that can think on the same level as a human.
The extraordinary technologies being pioneered by American innovators far exceed what was envisioned when the term “Artificial Intelligence” first came into use.
## . Is everyone really going to switch to “super intelligence” now? In a YouGov [poll](https://yougov.com/en-us/daily-results/20260928-5a780-1) conducted in late September, 53 percent thought the technology should be called “artificial intelligence,” while only 9 percent liked “super intelligence.”

item.title: Artificial intelligence (AI)-triggered rapid response notifications were associated with lower mortality among inpatients
item.description:
# Artificial intelligence (AI)-triggered rapid response notifications were associated with lower mortality among inpatients [October 2, 2026](https://www.2minutemedicine.com/artificial-intelligence-ai-triggered-rapid-response-notifications-were-associated-with-lower-mortality-among-inpatients/)
in [Artificial Intelligence](https://www.2minutemedicine.com/category/all/artificial-intelligence/), [Emergency](https://www.2minutemedicine.com/category/all/emergency-2/)
[Share on Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.2minutemedicine.com%2Fartificial-intelligence-ai-triggered-rapid-response-notifications-were-associated-with-lower-mortality-among-inpatients%2F) [Share on Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Artificial%20intelligence%20%28AI%29-triggered%20rapid%20response%20notifications%20were%20associated%20with%20lower%20mortality%20among%20inpatients&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.2minutemedicine.com%2Fartificial-intelligence-ai-triggered-rapid-response-notifications-were-associated-with-lower-mortality-among-inpatients%2F) [Share on Pinterest](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/create/bookmarklet/?pinFave=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.2minutemedicine.com%2Fartificial-intelligence-ai-triggered-rapid-response-notifications-were-associated-with-lower-mortality-among-inpatients%2F&media=https://www.2minutemedicine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/second%20batch%20featured/cardiology_covid_vaccination_rhythm_2_minute_medicine.webp&description=Artificial%20intelligence%20%28AI%29-triggered%20rapid%20response%20notifications%20were%20associated%20with%20lower%20mortality%20among%20inpatients)
**Nahass and colleagues evaluated the implementation of an AI-powered electronic alert system that automatically activated the rapid response team.**
**Automated rapid response team notifications were associated with lower inpatient deaths and more rapid response activations.**
## Go deeper into the evidence. **Study Rundown:** Newer machine-learning models, such as the Epic Deterioration Index (EDI), may reduce in-hospital mortality. The study found that unadjusted mortality decreased from 23.1% before implementation to 18.6% afterward, with an adjusted odds ratio of 0.82. This study demonstrated that integrating AI-powered deterioration predictions into clinical response workflows may improve outcomes among higher-risk patients.
### [Artificial intelligence (AI) capable of identifying uncommon gastrointestinal pathologies despite no targeted disease training](https://www.2minutemedicine.com/artificial-intelligence-ai-capable-of-identifying-uncommon-gastrointestinal-pathologies-despite-no-targeted-disease-training/) **In-Depth [prospective cohort]:** Adult admissions with an EDI score of at least 60 were enrolled across 11 hospital sites. 10,803 patients were included in the pre-implementation cohort, and 12,329 were included in the post-implementation cohort. A modified EDI excluding the Glasgow Coma Scale generated predictions every 15 minutes, and scores of at least 60 triggered RRT mobile notifications unless suppression criteria were applied (e.g., existing intensive or comfort care, recent alerts, or recent RRT events). Before implementation, scores were calculated but not used. Escalation was defined as transfer from acute to intermediate or intensive care, or from intermediate to intensive care. Deaths occurred in 2,500 pre-intervention patients versus 2,297 post-intervention patients, an absolute difference of −4.5 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], −5.6 to −3.5). The adjusted mortality odds ratio was 0.82 (95% CI, 0.74-0.91), while the adjusted RRT activation odds ratio was 1.74 (95% CI, 1.61–1.88). The mortality rate for the group just below the threshold (EDI 55–59) decreased from 2.9% to 2.3%, with an adjusted odds ratio of 0.99 (95% CI, 0.70-1.39). Meanwhile, the mortality rate for the group just above the threshold decreased from 5.5% to 3.8%, with an adjusted odds ratio of 0.86 (95% CI, 0.63 to 1.17). Only 46.6% of post-intervention encounters generated notifications. This study was limited by unequal seasonal distributions of the pre- and post-intervention phases, incomplete implementation at two hospitals, and uncertain generalizability beyond the sites studied. Nonetheless, this study provided evidence that connecting an AI-enabled prediction model in the EHR with real- time alerts to the clinical team could reduce mortality among admitted patients.

item.title: Rice University launching AI master's program
item.description:
#### The Brief - Rice University is launching a dedicated Master of Artificial Intelligence (MAI) degree next fall to help fill a demand for specialized AI engineers.
**HOUSTON** - As artificial intelligence continues to reshape workplaces and daily life, the demand for qualified engineers who can design, build, and deploy complex systems has reached an all-time high.
The university’s Department of Computer Science has announced a dedicated Master of Artificial Intelligence (MAI) program launching next fall.
